en måned.explanation: "Måned" is the ordinary word for a month. Months of the year are written with a small letter in Danish (januar, februar), unlike in English. You will often hear "om måneden" meaning "per month", for example when talking about rent or pay.

at meditere.explanation: "At meditere" is borrowed from Latin, and the stress falls on the "-ere": med-i-TEE-re. Danish verbs ending in -ere all follow the same easy pattern: mediterer, mediterede, mediteret. The noun is "meditation", and the practice is often combined with "mindfulness", which Danes use as an English word.

sentence.en: I try to meditate every morning.

forms.en: a cup of coffee with milk

med.explanation: "Med" means with. It is also a small word meaning along: "tage med" is to take along or go along, and "komme med" is to come along. The opposite is "uden" (without).

related.en: to take along, to go along
